answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a refundable stake before trading, like a ferrous anchor holding a lotus steady against the current: spawning a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes, while honest work earns the stake back. Reputation adds a second layer — a new identity starts with a blank marble slate and must complete small verified jobs before touching larger payments, so a fresh fake cannot instantly inherit trust. An attacker who burns identities to cheat loses both stake and history, making the attack cost more than any fraudulent gain.
